label: Freelance contract
text:
INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Independent Contractor Services Agreement (the "Agreement") is made effective as of October 12, 2026 (the "Effective Date") between Harbor & Pine Home Goods LLC, a Pennsylvania limited liability company ("Client"), and Alex Moreno, an individual doing business as Moreno Studio ("Contractor").

1. SERVICES. Contractor shall redesign Client's e-commerce website, including a new visual design system, homepage, collection page, product page, and cart page templates, and shall deliver all source design files and front-end code (the "Deliverables"), as further described in the Statement of Work attached as Exhibit A.

2. SCHEDULE. Contractor shall deliver final Deliverables no later than six (6) weeks after the Effective Date. Time is of the essence. If Contractor fails to deliver any Deliverable by its due date, Client may deduct $100.00 per calendar day of delay from the Fee, regardless of the cause of the delay.

3. REVISIONS. Contractor shall make all revisions requested by Client until Client is fully satisfied with the Deliverables. There is no limit on the number of revision rounds included in the Fee.

4. ACCEPTANCE. Client shall review each Deliverable and may accept or reject it in Client's sole discretion. A Deliverable is accepted only when Client gives written notice of acceptance. Client has no obligation to accept any Deliverable within a specific time.

5. FEE. Client shall pay Contractor a fixed fee of $8,500.00 (the "Fee") for the Services. The Fee includes all revisions, meetings, travel, software, stock assets, fonts, and other expenses. Contractor shall not be reimbursed for any expenses.

6. PAYMENT TERMS. Contractor shall invoice Client upon Client's written acceptance of all final Deliverables. Client shall pay each undisputed invoice within sixty (60) days of receipt. No deposit or partial payment shall be due before final acceptance. Client may withhold payment of any amount it disputes in good faith.

7. OWNERSHIP OF WORK. All Deliverables, and all drafts, concepts, sketches, and other work product created by Contractor in connection with this Agreement, whether or not used by Client, are "works made for hire" and shall be the sole property of Client from the moment of creation. To the extent any such work is not a work made for hire, Contractor hereby assigns to Client all right, title, and interest in it. Contractor also grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to use any tools, code libraries, templates, or materials that Contractor owned before the Effective Date and incorporated into the Deliverables.

8. PORTFOLIO. Contractor shall not display, publish, or reference the Deliverables, Client's name, or Client's logo in any portfolio, website, social media post, or case study without Client's prior written consent.

9. TERMINATION. Client may terminate this Agreement at any time, for any reason, upon written notice to Contractor. Upon termination, Client shall pay Contractor only for Deliverables that Client has accepted in writing before the date of termination, prorated against the Fee, and Client shall own all work product created through the date of termination. Contractor may terminate this Agreement only if Client fails to pay an undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days after written notice of non-payment.

10. NON-COMPETITION. During the term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months afterward, Contractor shall not provide design or development services to any company that sells home goods, furniture, or home decor products online.

11. NON-SOLICITATION. During the term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months afterward, Contractor shall not solicit or accept work from any of Client's vendors, suppliers, or wholesale customers.

12. INDEMNIFICATION. Contractor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Client and its members, managers, and employees from and against any and all claims, losses, damages, and expenses, including attorney's fees, arising out of or relating to the Services or the Deliverables.

13. LIMITATION OF CLIENT LIABILITY. In no event shall Client's total liability under this Agreement exceed the amount of the Fee actually paid to Contractor.

14. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR. Contractor is an independent contractor and not an employee of Client. Contractor is responsible for all taxes, insurance, and benefits. Contractor shall carry general liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and shall name Client as an additional insured.

15. CONFIDENTIALITY. Contractor shall keep confidential all non-public information about Client's business, customers, sales, and plans, during the term of this Agreement and for five (5) years afterward.

16. GOVERNING LAW AND VENUE. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. Any dispute shall be brought exclusively in the courts located in Berks County, Pennsylvania.

17. ENTIRE AGREEMENT. This Agreement and Exhibit A are the entire agreement between the parties and supersede all prior proposals, quotes, and communications, including any proposal or estimate submitted by Contractor.

CLIENT: Harbor & Pine Home Goods LLC
By: Morgan Hale, Managing Member

CONTRACTOR: Alex Moreno, d/b/a Moreno Studio

reading.title: Website redesign contract between Moreno Studio and Harbor & Pine Home Goods
reading.summary: This is a fixed-price contract for you to redesign Harbor & Pine's online store for $8,500.00, with all expenses on you. Payment comes only after the client accepts everything in writing, the client can take as long as it wants to accept, and then it has 60 days to pay. The client can also ask for unlimited revisions, cancel at any time without paying for unaccepted work, and bar you from all online home goods clients for 12 months. The effective date of October 12, 2026 has already passed, so the 6-week deadline is already running.

key_terms.label: Fee
key_terms.quote: Client shall pay Contractor a fixed fee of $8,500.00 (the "Fee") for the Services.

key_terms.label: Expenses
key_terms.quote: Contractor shall not be reimbursed for any expenses.

key_terms.label: Deadline
key_terms.quote: Contractor shall deliver final Deliverables no later than six (6) weeks after the Effective Date.

key_terms.label: Late deduction
key_terms.quote: Client may deduct $100.00 per calendar day of delay from the Fee, regardless of the cause of the delay.

key_terms.label: Payment timing
key_terms.quote: Client shall pay each undisputed invoice within sixty (60) days of receipt.

key_terms.label: Non-compete
key_terms.quote: During the term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months afterward, Contractor shall not provide design or development services

key_terms.label: Insurance you must carry
key_terms.quote: Contractor shall carry general liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and shall name Client as an additional insured.

key_terms.label: Confidentiality
key_terms.quote: during the term of this Agreement and for five (5) years afterward.

push_back.title: No limit on acceptance or revisions
push_back.why: The client decides alone whether your work is acceptable, has no deadline to decide, and can ask for unlimited revisions. Since you only get paid after acceptance, the client can delay your pay indefinitely.
push_back.ask: Can we cap revisions at 2 rounds per deliverable, and treat a deliverable as accepted if you don't reject it in writing with reasons within 5 business days?
push_back.quote: Client has no obligation to accept any Deliverable within a specific time.

push_back.title: No deposit and slow payment
push_back.why: You carry all the work and costs up front and may not see money until well after 60 days past final acceptance. Common practice for design work is a deposit plus milestone payments.
push_back.ask: Can we do 50% up front, 25% on design approval, and 25% on final delivery, each due within 15 days of invoice?
push_back.quote: No deposit or partial payment shall be due before final acceptance.

push_back.title: Cancellation leaves you unpaid
push_back.why: The client can cancel for any reason, pay only for work it has formally accepted, and still keep all your unfinished work. You can only leave if they fail to pay, and they owe nothing until acceptance anyway.
push_back.ask: If you terminate, can you pay for all work done up to that date, with ownership of that work passing only after payment?
push_back.quote: Upon termination, Client shall pay Contractor only for Deliverables that Client has accepted in writing before the date of termination

push_back.title: Broad 12-month non-compete
push_back.why: This bars you from working for any online home goods, furniture, or decor seller for a year, which could cut off a large part of your market for an $8,500 job. Whether this is enforceable depends on where you live, so check the rules there.
push_back.ask: Can we remove the non-compete, or limit it to a short list of named direct competitors for 3 months? Can the non-solicitation clause cover only soliciting, not accepting, work?
push_back.quote: Contractor shall not provide design or development services to any company that sells home goods, furniture, or home decor products online.

push_back.title: Late penalty even when it isn't your fault
push_back.why: You lose $100 a day even if the delay comes from the client's slow feedback, missing content, or endless revisions. Over 85 days it would wipe out the whole fee.
push_back.ask: Can the deadline move day-for-day with any delay caused by you, and can the late deduction be capped at 10% of the fee?
push_back.quote: regardless of the cause of the delay

good_to_know.title: You cover all claims, with no limit
good_to_know.why: Indemnify means you pay the client's costs and legal fees for any claim tied to your work, even claims you didn't cause. There is no cap, while the client's own liability is capped.
good_to_know.quote: Contractor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Client and its members, managers, and employees from and against any and all claims, losses, damages, and expenses, including attorney's fees

good_to_know.title: Client's liability is capped at what it paid you
good_to_know.why: If the client never pays, its liability cap could be zero. Your liability has no cap.
good_to_know.quote: In no event shall Client's total liability under this Agreement exceed the amount of the Fee actually paid to Contractor.

good_to_know.title: The client owns even unused drafts and gets your tools
good_to_know.why: Rejected concepts become theirs from the moment you make them. Any code, templates, or tools you already owned get a permanent free license to the client if you use them.
good_to_know.quote: Contractor also grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to use any tools, code libraries, templates, or materials that Contractor owned before the Effective Date

good_to_know.title: No portfolio use without permission
good_to_know.why: You can't show this work or even name the client without written consent. Ask for portfolio rights after launch if this matters to you.
good_to_know.quote: Contractor shall not display, publish, or reference the Deliverables, Client's name, or Client's logo in any portfolio, website, social media post, or case study without Client's prior written consent.

good_to_know.title: Your proposal is wiped out
good_to_know.why: Anything you promised or limited in your quote, like revision rounds or scope, no longer counts unless it is written into this contract or Exhibit A.
good_to_know.quote: supersede all prior proposals, quotes, and communications, including any proposal or estimate submitted by Contractor.

good_to_know.title: Disputes go to court in Berks County, Pennsylvania
good_to_know.why: If you live far away, any lawsuit would mean traveling there.
good_to_know.quote: Any dispute shall be brought exclusively in the courts located in Berks County, Pennsylvania.

dates.label: Effective date
dates.when: Already passed, so the schedule is already running
dates.quote: is made effective as of October 12, 2026 (the "Effective Date")

dates.label: Final deliverables due
dates.when: 6 weeks after October 12, 2026. $100 a day comes off your fee after this.
dates.quote: Contractor shall deliver final Deliverables no later than six (6) weeks after the Effective Date.

dates.label: Your right to quit for non-payment
dates.when: 30 days after you send written notice that an undisputed invoice is unpaid
dates.quote: Contractor may terminate this Agreement only if Client fails to pay an undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days after written notice of non-payment.

dates.label: Non-compete and non-solicitation end
dates.quote: During the term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months afterward, Contractor shall not solicit or accept work from any of Client's vendors, suppliers, or wholesale customers.

before_you_sign: Ask for Exhibit A, the Statement of Work, and read it, because it was not included.
Ask to change the effective date to the day you sign so the 6-week clock doesn't start early.
Get a quote for $1,000,000 general liability insurance and add that cost to your price.
List any code, templates, or fonts you plan to reuse, and decide if you're fine licensing them forever.
Check the rules where you live on whether a 12-month non-compete like this one can be enforced.
Put any promises from your original proposal into the contract in writing.

email.subject: Questions on the website redesign agreement
email.body:
Hi Morgan,

Thanks for sending the contractor agreement for the Harbor & Pine redesign. Before I sign, I'd like to discuss a few terms:

1. Acceptance and revisions: Can we limit revisions to 2 rounds per deliverable and treat work as accepted if it isn't rejected in writing within 5 business days?
2. Payment: Can we do 50% up front, 25% at design approval, and 25% at final delivery, each due within 15 days of invoice?
3. Termination: If the agreement ends early, can I be paid for all work done to that date, with ownership passing on payment?
4. Non-compete: Can we remove it or limit it to a few named direct competitors for 3 months? Can the non-solicitation cover soliciting only, not accepting work?
5. Late deduction: Can the deadline move with any delays on your side, and can the deduction be capped at 10% of the fee?

I'd also like a copy of Exhibit A, and to set the effective date to the signing date.

Thank you,
[Your name]
